# Continual-ARC task-efce8044 — solved

## Verified rule
Remove sparse one-cell outliers/noise from a scene of solid rectangular color regions on a uniform background. Keep the original background and all solid rectangular regions, even when their fill color is the background value (as in the demo's large color-8 field patches). A stray pixel lying inside an otherwise uniform rectangle is replaced by that rectangle's fill; a stray pixel outside regions is set to the background. Distinguish region membership from color alone: colors used for outliers may also be legitimate rectangle colors.

## Demonstration evidence
Demo input/output was 21x22 with background color 8. The output preserved the rectangular patches (colors 2, 3, and 5, including patches of color 2 within the large color-8 field) and removed all scattered single-cell marks of colors 6 and 7. A 7 inside a color-2 rectangle was restored to 2; other scattered marks became background 8. This establishes cleanup of isolated specks while preserving rectangular regions.

## Accepted test evidence
Test input was 19x12, background 0. Accepted output kept the solid rectangles/patches, including color-9 and color-7 areas and all the color-1 regions. Noise was removed or repaired according to its location:
- 7 at (row 5, cols 0–1) and (row 6, cols 0–1) were genuine color-7 rectangle pixels; preserve them.
- 6 at row 7, col 5 and 4 at row 17, col 6 were inside color-1 regions, so became 1.
- 4 at row 10, col 9 was inside a color-1 patch, so became 1.
- isolated 2 at row 7, col 0 and 3 at row 11, col 0 were outside solid regions, so became background 0.
- Genuine blocks remained unchanged: color 9 at rows 0–3 cols 0–3; color 7 at rows 5–6 cols 0–1; color 1 patches at rows 2–7 cols 5–10, rows 8–9 cols 1–3, rows 12–17 cols 2–6, and the color-1 patches around rows 10–12 and 15–18 cols 8–9.

## Practical approach
1. Identify the uniform background and all coherent, solid rectangular color patches.
2. For each anomalous singleton, determine whether it falls inside a patch (restore that patch's fill) or outside (replace with background).
3. Preserve legitimate rectangle cells, even if a color also appears in noise elsewhere.
4. Validate output dimensions and each row length before submitting.
